evidence.quoted_text:
"manager_restarted": (
            (((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
             .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                 .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            and bool(((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and bool(((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")),
evidence.reason: The manager_restarted check only proves that the manager PID and invocation ID differ between the two manager snapshots. It never requires both snapshots to come from the same guest boot. If the guest reboots between those observations, the manager can restart as a side effect of the reboot and still satisfy the changed PID/invocation-ID checks, so the report falsely records an isolated manager restart. Requiring both manager snapshots to have nonempty equal boot IDs is a routine correctness repair, not a contract conflict or scope enlargement.
